Topics · Who was Muhammad?

Who was Muhammad, and why believe him?

No belief asked. Three questions the Quran raises: how he lived, what he gained, who holds him to account.

Part 1 of 3

﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَعِظُكُم بِوَٰحِدَةٍ ۖ أَن تَقُومُوا۟ لِلَّهِ مَثْنَىٰ وَفُرَٰدَىٰ ثُمَّ تَتَفَكَّرُوا۟ ۚ مَا بِصَاحِبِكُم مِّن جِنَّةٍ ۚ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ لَّكُم بَيْنَ يَدَىْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "I only advise you of one [thing] - that you stand for Allāh, [seeking truth] in pairs and individually, and then give thought." There is not in your companion any madness. He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment.

Quran · Saba 34:46

How do you judge a man who says he is a messenger? Not by the enthusiasm of a crowd, since crowds can follow or oppose without thinking. The verse asks for a simple method: stand before God, alone or with one other person, then think. It does not ask you to believe. It asks you to weigh. That is why this app shows you no counts and no streaks. The judging is yours, in quiet.

A question for you

How do you usually judge someone who makes a great claim?

If you sayBy what they gain from it.
ThenA good measure, and the next part will use it.
If you sayBy their life before it.
ThenThat is exactly what the next part asks about.
If you sayBy who holds them to account.
ThenKeep that measure for the last part.

Part 2 of 3

﴿قُل لَّوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَا تَلَوْتُهُۥ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَآ أَدْرَىٰكُم بِهِۦ ۖ فَقَدْ لَبِثْتُ فِيكُمْ عُمُرًا مِّن قَبْلِهِۦٓ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "If Allāh had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you, for I had remained among you a lifetime before it.[516] Then will you not reason?"

Translator's notes

[516] The Prophet (ﷺ) lived among his people forty years before receiving any revelation.

Quran · Yunus 10:16

﴿أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَى ٱللَّهُ ۖ فَبِهُدَىٰهُمُ ٱقْتَدِهْ ۗ قُل لَّآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْرًا ۖ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرَىٰ لِلْعَـٰلَمِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Those are the ones whom Allāh has guided, so from their guidance take an example. Say, "I ask of you for it [i.e., this message] no payment. It is not but a reminder for the worlds."

Quran · Al-An'am 6:90

A false claimant often leaves marks: a history of claiming, a hunger for money. The first verse offers evidence his own people could check: I lived among you a lifetime before this. The second gives another measure: I ask you for no wage. A person can be sincere and mistaken, but the first question is whether this is a man lying for himself.

A question for you

Which explanation seems strongest for a life like this?

If you sayHe told the truth.
ThenOne step remains: truthful and from God, or truthful and mistaken? The next part comes closer to that.
If you saySincere, but mistaken.
ThenThat is the strongest objection, and sincerity alone does not answer it. See what the next part does.
If you sayHe drew on others.
ThenThat view has its own Step, which sets it before the texts.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيْنَا بَعْضَ ٱلْأَقَاوِيلِ٤٤ لَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُ بِٱلْيَمِينِ٤٥ ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنَا مِنْهُ ٱلْوَتِينَ٤٦ فَمَا مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَـٰجِزِينَ٤٧﴾

Translation of the meaning

And if he [i.e., Muḥammad] had made up about Us some [false] sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand;[1745] Then We would have cut from him the aorta.[1746] And there is no one of you who could prevent [Us] from him.

Translator's notes

[1745] Another interpretation is "by [Our] right hand," i.e., Allāh would have exacted revenge with might and power.

[1746] Causing immediate death.

Quran · Al-Haqqah 69:44-47

﴿قُلْ مَا كُنتُ بِدْعًا مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ وَمَآ أَدْرِى مَا يُفْعَلُ بِى وَلَا بِكُمْ ۖ إِنْ أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا مَا يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "I am not something new among the messengers,[1479] nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow that which is revealed to me, and I am not but a clear warner."

Translator's notes

[1479] i.e., I am neither the first messenger to be sent, nor do I bring something different from the other messengers.

Quran · Al-Ahqaf 46:9

You might expect a man who invented a book to speak for God to make it only raise and protect him. These verses go another way: had he forged anything in Our name, We would have seized him. The text makes its speaker the first to stand under its account. The other verse says: I do not know what will be done with me. A sceptic may say this too could win trust. So the argument is cumulative, and no one verse decides it. The judging stays with you.

A question for you

What more would you need in order to weigh this fairly?

If you sayTo read the Quran itself.
ThenThat is what the book invites: see the test it sets for itself.
If you sayTo know why the Quran corrects its Prophet.
ThenThat is the next question along this road.
If you sayTo see what other books say.
ThenThat has its own Step too, ready whenever you want it.

Your reflection

What is the first thing you would ask this man if you could sit with him?
